decisions.quote: We used an online survey with a translated version of the original questionnaire, as well as an extension scenario. The final sample included 436 participants.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding agree that this study is a replication that collected new survey data from 436 Brazilian participants using a translated version of the original questionnaire.

decisions.quote: Tykocinski, O. E., Pittman, T. S., & Tuttle, E. E. (1995). Inaction inertia: Foregoing future benefits as a result of an initial failure to act.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind target 0 identify Tykocinski, Pittman, and Tuttle (1995) as the replicated original study; the DOI discrepancy is merely a double-slash formatting variant in the reference list.

decisions.quote: All scenarios presented significant differences between conditions (p-values < 0.001; ϵ² ranging from 0.06 to 0.22), except for the Frequent flyer scenario (p-value = 0.073; ϵ² = 0.01).
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly characterize their findings against Tykocinski et al. (1995) as a partial replication, replicating 6 of 12 between-condition comparisons across three of the four original scenarios while finding no significant effect in the Frequent flyer scenario.

decisions.quote: Comparison of effect sizes between ours and Chen et al. (2021) replications.
decisions.reason: The study translates and directly re-tests the four scenarios from Tykocinski et al. (1995); Chen et al. (2021) is an earlier replication of the same original protocol used for power calculations and effect-size comparisons rather than an independent original target.
